build-projects.description: Measure the repository and gate the limits it declares over itself. An nx:noop aggregator, the way every project's `build-projects` is. `dependsOn` names `codometer` alone rather than inheriting the targetDefault's `build`: the root project builds nothing, and this run measures source. It exists so 👷 Make Projects reaches the repository itself — the workflows under .github belong to no project, so without this nothing gates their comment budgets.

callidescope.description: Publish the workspace call-stack trace: every project's README block, the mermaid diagram, and the JSON report. The only configuration left is `write` — depth checking now runs through the inferred per-project `callidescope-gate` target, a dependency of `guard-code`, scoped by `nx affected` in the 💂 Guard check and `configuration/lint-staged.config.ts`, so a pull request and a commit gate the projects a change actually touched rather than the whole workspace. This target still stays out of `lint-code`'s `dependsOn` for the reason it always did, unchanged by that split because `write` is exactly the configuration that remains: Nx forwards an explicit configuration down `dependsOn`, so a target reachable from there would take `write` from `lint-code --configuration=write` and publish the report from a branch. `defaultConfiguration` is `write`, the only configuration left, so a bare `nx run codebase:callidescope` does what `:write` does. Publishing did not fan out the way gating did: one JSON report and one set of README blocks are what the whole workspace needs, and computing either per project would mean rebuilding the same call graph many times for one merged artifact, where gating benefits from being scoped to what changed and publishing does not. Four traced call-graph roots carry no gate of their own and never will, because a gate is inferred onto an Nx project and none of them is one. `configuration/` carries its own `tsconfig.json` and so is traced, measuring depth 3; three fixture roots under `packages/ic-suite/codependix/codependix-examples/examples/` are the same case at depth 0. All four keep being traced and published here on the default branch, so a regression in any of them still lands in the report; it only stops failing a pull request. The workspace root is a fifth gap of a different kind and is not one of the four: `configuration/.callidescopeignore` drops it as a project, for the reason recorded there, so the loose maintenance scripts it once owned are traced by nothing at all — which is also why the root project is skipped from gate inference, its scope being the workspace itself. The README glob is an input because `write` splices into those files: without it, a hand-edited report replays a cached run.

check-catalog-manifests.description: Enforce catalog: protocol for external dependencies in workspace package manifests

check-lockfile.description: Verify that pnpm-lock.yaml is in sync with package.json files

check-readme-projects.description: Verify the root README links to every workspace project

codependix.description: Export every configured Nx, NestJS, and file-import dependency graph, and gate the rules those graphs are judged against. Two configurations and no third, mirroring `codebase:callidescope` and `codebase:codometer`. `guard-code` depends on this target and forwards its configuration here, so `guard-code:check` — the 💂 Guard check on every pull request, and the pre-commit hook — runs `check`, and a local `guard-code:write` runs `write`. `check` runs `--check boundaries`, which reads no destination and writes nothing — a broken boundary is caused by the branch and fixed by it, so it gates every pull request, beside the inferred per-project `callidescope-gate` target that checks call-stack depth. The command line also accepts `--check reports`, which is what a bare `--check` used to mean, and nothing runs it: a configured export moves with the workspace it describes and would fail every branch that changed a project graph rather than anything the branch itself did. The release workflow runs `write`, after `callidescope` and the module-graph synchronization have run, so a project's `## 🕸️ Codependix` anchor reflects the same commit those write. The README glob is an input because `write` splices Markdown into anchor blocks placed by hand in those files.

codometer.description: Measure the whole repository: `check` gates the limits it declares over itself, chiefly the 128-word comment budgets declared per language, and `write` writes its README.md statistics badges. The two flags name two findings on opposite sides of a pull request, the same split callidescope makes. `check` reads no output destination and writes nothing, which is what makes it safe on a branch — a breached budget is something the branch did. `write` passes `--output-markdown` with no path, since the workspace configuration already declares README.md as its markdown destination. Report staleness is deliberately not checked: those badges are written on main by the release workflow, so every branch would fail for being behind rather than for anything it did. `dependsOn` is written out as an empty list rather than left to the `codometer` targetDefault, which depends on `build`: a per-project run measures compiled output and must wait for it, while this one measures source and would otherwise wait on every build in the workspace — slow, and circular, since the tools it would be waiting for are measured by it. The two are deliberately different and must not be collapsed into one. `options.env.SWC_NODE_PROJECT` is written out for the same reason: the `codometer` targetDefault points it at `../../configuration/tsconfig.json`, relative to a per-project run's own `{projectRoot}` cwd, and this target already overrides `cwd` back to `{workspaceRoot}` — merging the targetDefault's `env` in unchanged would resolve two directories above the repository entirely. `@swc-node/register`'s ESM hook needs this pointed at a real tsconfig to load `codometer-cli` at all, since it resolves `SWC_NODE_PROJECT` as `<cwd>/tsconfig.json` with no upward search. This is also the only run that reaches the workflows under .github, which belong to no project, so no per-project run ever measures them.

commit-msg.description: Run the commit-msg git hook script (commitlint). Pass the commit message file via --edit=<path>.

commitlint.description: Validate commit message format with commitlint. The commit-msg hook calls the binary directly to avoid a project graph build; this target is for manual use.

conformetry-generate.description: Run the conformetry generate command from the workspace root

options.command: pnpm exec nx run conformetry-cli:start -- generate {args}

eslint.description: Lint workspace root files with ESLint — config files, scripts, documentation, infrastructure, and every markdown file in the workspace. That trailing `**/*.md` is what gives `project-structure/folder-structure` reach over markdown paths, and it is a workspace-wide glob rather than a list of directories on purpose: an enumerated list only judges the directories somebody remembered to add, so it would not have caught openwiki/ — the undeclared directory that motivated the rule — and would not catch the next one. Markdown inside a project is judged twice, here and by that project's own eslint target, which costs a second and reports the same answer.

fallow.description: Run all fallow static analyses (dead-code, duplicates, health) in advisory mode

fallow-audit.description: Fallow audit gate (new-only regression check on changed code) — advisory

fallow-dead-code.description: Fallow dead-code analysis (unused files, exports, types, dependencies, unresolved imports) — a `lint-code` gate beside `knip`, whose findings it deliberately mirrors: `configuration/fallow.config.jsonc` carries the same entry points, the same per-file report suppressions, and the same ignored dependencies as `configuration/knip.config.ts`, so a finding one reports the other reports too. The severities `knip` also fails on are `error` in that config; the rest stay `warn` and belong to `fallow-health` and `fallow-duplicates`, which are still advisory. The `write` configuration is identical to `check` because there is nothing to write: removing what this finds is `fallow-fix`, which stays manual-only.

fallow-duplicates.description: Fallow strict duplication analysis (config-driven) with threshold gating

fallow-fix.description: ⚠️  MANUAL-ONLY (write config): removes unused exports/deps from source files — never include in automated pipelines. Use check config for safe dry-run preview.

fallow-health.description: Fallow code health analysis (complexity, hotspots, maintainability) — advisory

gitleaks.description: Detect hardcoded secrets in git history using Gitleaks (detection only). The ci-incremental configuration scopes the scan to NX_BASE..NX_HEAD instead of full history, for push/pull_request/merge_group events where the weekly ci scan already covers everything older.

install-skills.description: Restore the skills listed in skills-lock.json from their source repositories into the gitignored .agents/skills/<name>/ folders. Also runs from postinstall; the force configuration re-restores skills that are already present.

check.command: jscpd --config configuration/jscpd.config.json --no-tips --reporters console,threshold applications packages tools scripts configuration infrastructure || true

jscpd.description: Run jscpd duplicate-code reporting and threshold status in advisory mode (never fails CI).

knip.description: Check for unused files, dependencies, and exports in workspace root only

lint-staged.description: Run lint-staged on staged files (invoked by the pre-commit git hook)

markdown-lint.description: Lint markdown files in workspace root (agents, scripts, documentation, infrastructure). Reaches .agents/ so this repository's own skills are linted like any other documentation; the vendored skills in skills-lock.json are excluded per skill in the markdownlint configuration. The inputs enumerate exactly the globs the command lints, plus the markdownlint configuration and shared-globals — the latter carries pnpm-lock.yaml, so a markdownlint upgrade cannot replay a cached pass. The workspace-wide default input is deliberately absent: it resolves to {projectRoot}/**/* for the root project, which made every root-owned file the tool never reads invalidate this cache. The vendored-skills negations then drop the 59 skills markdownlint already ignores, so editing one of them no longer busts the cache for nothing.

openwiki.description: Update OpenWiki content from code using the OpenWiki CLI (prints changes).

openwiki-update.description: Update OpenWiki content from code using the OpenWiki CLI (prints changes).

oxfmt.description: Format workspace root files with oxfmt (config files, scripts, documentation, infrastructure)

oxlint.description: Run Oxlint on workspace root files — config files, scripts, documentation, infrastructure, and the devcontainer sync scripts. That last path is named because the others hold no TypeScript at all today: `scripts/` went shell-only when the two dead root scripts were deleted, and oxlint exits non-zero when its paths match nothing, so a target covering only empty directories fails rather than passing vacuously. The devcontainer scripts are real TypeScript that nothing else here was linting.

write.command: jq 'del(.pnpm.overrides)' package.json > package.temporary.json && mv package.temporary.json package.json && pnpm update --no-frozen-lockfile && pnpm audit --fix --ignore-unfixable; pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile

pnpm-audit.description: Scan for fixable security vulnerabilities (check, which passes when the advisory registry is unreachable) or clean stale overrides and re-fix (write)

dump-literature.command: PGPASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-postgres} pg_dump -h ${POSTGRES_HOST:-localhost} -p ${POSTGRES_PORT:-5432} -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres} -t authors -t lines -t texts -t tokens -Fc -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-postgres} -f data/literature.dump

restore-literature.command: PGPASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-postgres} pg_restore -h ${POSTGRES_HOST:-localhost} -p ${POSTGRES_PORT:-5432} -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-postgres} -c -1 -t authors -t lines -t texts -t tokens data/literature.dump

pre-push.description: Run the pre-push git hook script (branch name validation).

prettier.description: Format workspace root files with Prettier (excluding NX projects)

options.command: if [ -n "$PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER" ]; then NODE_OPTIONS='' node --import @swc-node/register/esm-register tools/synchronization/src/main.ts pull-request-labels write; else echo "Skipping label reconciliation"; fi

pnpm exec nx affected --target=secure-code --parallel=4 && if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ] || [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then pnpm exec nx run codebase:gitleaks:ci; else pnpm exec nx run codebase:gitleaks:ci-incremental; fi

shellcheck.description: Lint the workspace's own shell: every script under scripts/ and .devcontainer/, and the three husky hooks, which carry no extension and so are named one by one. The file list comes from `git ls-files`, whose `*` crosses directories, so a new script is linted without editing this target. Two shell files stay out on purpose: notepads/notepad.sh is a scratch list of commands rather than a script, and the codometer-examples corpus is a measurement fixture whose content its tests count. The installed skills under .agents/ are owned upstream and stay out too. configuration/.shellcheckrc is passed explicitly, since shellcheck only searches each script's own directory and its parents, and the minimum severity is set here because an rc file cannot set it: `style` is the lowest, so nothing is filtered out. pyproject.toml and uv.lock are inputs because they pin shellcheck itself: without them, an upgrade replays a cached pass and stops linting. Defined here rather than in nx.json targetDefaults because no other project owns shell scripts.

options.command: uv run shellcheck --rcfile configuration/.shellcheckrc --severity=style $(git ls-files -- '.devcontainer/*.sh' 'scripts/*.sh' configuration/.husky/commit-msg configuration/.husky/pre-commit configuration/.husky/pre-push)

write.command: pnpm dlx sherif@1.10.0 -p applications/JimmyPaolini --fix --no-install && nx run codebase:oxfmt:write

sherif.description: Lint codebase for consistent package.json conventions

spell-check.description: Check spelling in every workspace root file no project owns (configuration, documentation, infrastructure, notepads, openwiki, planning, scripts, and the .agents, .devcontainer, .github, and .vscode directories). Reaches .agents/ so this repository's own skills are spell-checked like any other documentation; the vendored skills in skills-lock.json are excluded per skill in the cspell configuration. The inputs enumerate exactly the globs the command checks, plus the cspell configuration and dictionaries and shared-globals — the latter carries pnpm-lock.yaml, so a cspell upgrade cannot replay a cached pass. The workspace-wide default input is deliberately absent: it resolves to {projectRoot}/**/* for the root project, which made every root-owned file the tool never reads invalidate this cache. The vendored-skills negations then drop the 59 skills cspell already ignores, so editing one of them no longer busts the cache for nothing.

sync-vscode-extensions.description: Validate that VS Code extensions are synchronized between .vscode/extensions.json and both devcontainer configurations (check) or sync them (write)

sync-vscode-settings.description: Validate that VS Code Machine settings contain all workspace settings (check) or merge workspace settings into Machine settings (write)

write.command: pnpm exec syncpack fix --config configuration/syncpack.config.cjs && nx run codebase:oxfmt:write

syncpack.description: Check dependency version consistency across packages (check) or fix mismatches (write)

trivy-config.description: Scan Terraform infrastructure code for misconfigurations using Trivy. Identical to what the Secure Code workflow runs, so a local run reproduces CI exactly. Requires trivy on PATH (the devcontainer installs it; otherwise `brew install trivy`).

options.command: trivy config infrastructure/terraform --format table --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --exit-code 1 --ignorefile configuration/trivyignore

type-coverage.description: Check TypeScript type coverage for workspace root (minimum 95%)

validate-branch-name.description: Validate the current branch name against the configured naming convention. The pre-push hook calls the binary directly to avoid a project graph build; this target is for manual use.

options.command: if [ -n "$BRANCH_NAME" ]; then validate-branch-name -t "$BRANCH_NAME"; else validate-branch-name; fi

if [ -n "$PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER" ] && [ "$GITHUB_ACTOR" != "dependabot[bot]" ]; then gh pr view "$PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER" --json body -q .body > pull_request_body.md && NODE_OPTIONS='' node --import @swc-node/register/esm-register tools/validation/src/main.ts pull-request-body pull_request_body.md && rm pull_request_body.md; else echo "Skipping PR body validation"; fi

if [ -n "$PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER" ]; then NODE_OPTIONS='' node --import @swc-node/register/esm-register tools/validation/src/main.ts pull-request-release-significance "$PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER"; else echo "Skipping release significance"; fi
if [ -n "$PULL_REQUEST_TITLE" ]; then echo "$PULL_REQUEST_TITLE" | commitlint --config configuration/commitlint.config.ts; else echo "Skipping PR title validation"; fi

vulture.description: Check root-level Python utilities for dead code

yaml-lint.description: Lint the workspace-root YAML no project reaches: the GitHub Actions workflows, composite action, and issue templates, the devcontainer and infrastructure compose files, the Helm chart and its values, the shared cspell and yamllint configuration, and the pnpm workspace file. The generated pnpm-lock.yaml is left out on purpose, and the Helm templates are skipped by the `**/templates/` ignore in yamllint.yaml because their Go template directives are not valid YAML. The installed skills under .agents/ are owned upstream and stay out. pyproject.toml and uv.lock are inputs because they pin yamllint itself: without them, a yamllint upgrade replays a cached pass and stops linting. Defined here rather than in the nx.json targetDefaults entry, which is filtered to language tags this project does not carry.

options.command: uv run yamllint -c configuration/yamllint.yaml .devcontainer .github configuration/cspell.config.yaml configuration/yamllint.yaml infrastructure pnpm-workspace.yaml
